security_engineering.concept_summary: Two-Factor Authentication (2FA) requires providing identity evidence from two distinct authentication categories. Presenting multiple credentials from the same category does not qualify as 2FA.
security_engineering.analogy: Like entering a bank vault that requires both a secret combination (Knowledge) and a physical brass key (Possession), not two separate combinations.

actors.label: Alice
actors.description: Enterprise employee authenticating to internal systems

steps.action: Submits primary account password
Challenges for second verification credential
Submits childhood pet answer
Rejects session: duplicate knowledge factors
Submits primary account password
Dispatches cryptographic challenge nonce
Signs nonce via physical FIDO2 key touch
Validates distinct categories and issues JWT session

explanation_lines.note: Rejects multiple factors from identical category

comparison_table.option_b: Vulnerable to phishing and credential stuffing

comparison_table.option_a: Hardware token, FIDO2 key, TOTP app
comparison_table.option_b: Requires physical access or registered device

takeaways: 2FA requires credentials from distinct categories, not two passwords.
SMS OTP is vulnerable to SIM-swapping; WebAuthn/FIDO2 is phishing-resistant.
In interviews, emphasize knowledge, possession, and inherence clearly.
common_mistakes: Confusing 2-step verification (two passwords) with genuine multi-factor authentication.
Assuming SMS OTP provides equal security to hardware-backed FIDO2 keys.
Failing to articulate the three foundational authentication categories.

data_engineering.concept_summary: Broadcast Joins eliminate costly network data shuffling by transmitting a small lookup table entirely to all worker nodes executing distributed join queries.
data_engineering.analogy: Like handing a printed price cheat-sheet to every cashier rather than forcing all cashiers to walk across the store to read a single central ledger.

actors.label: Spark Driver
actors.description: Cluster coordinator planning physical execution DAGs

scenario.title: Distributed Join Execution: Shuffled Hash Join vs Broadcast Join

steps.action: Shuffles gigabytes of partition data across physical network
steps.annotation: High network saturation and shuffle spill

steps.action: Reciprocates shuffle partition records
Reports out-of-memory executor failure from shuffle skew
steps.annotation: Join failed due to partition skew

steps.action: Replicates small lookup table into worker memory cache
Replicates same lookup table into worker memory cache
Completes local in-memory hash join in milliseconds

code_sample.code:
from pyspark.sql.functions import broadcast

# Broadcast small dimension table to avoid heavy shuffle
large_events = spark.read.parquet('s3://lake/events/')
small_countries = spark.read.parquet('s3://lake/countries/')

joined_df = large_events.join(
    broadcast(small_countries),
    on='country_code',
    how='inner'
)

explanation_lines.note: Wraps small table with broadcast() hint
Executes local map-side join without network shuffle

comparison_table.option_a: High: O(N) records exchanged over cluster network
comparison_table.option_b: Zero: Small table replicated once to executors

comparison_table.option_a: Negligible: Driver does not collect table data
comparison_table.option_b: High: Driver collects table before broadcast

takeaways: Use broadcast joins when one table comfortably fits in executor RAM.
Default Spark threshold is 10MB; tune via spark.sql.autoBroadcastJoinThreshold.
Beware driver OutOfMemory errors if broadcasting tables larger than driver heap.
common_mistakes: Broadcasting a large table that exhausts driver or executor JVM heap.
Overlooking data skew in skewed keys where broadcast cannot apply.
Assuming broadcast join works on full outer joins (outer requires shuffle).

ai_tech_interview.concept_summary: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) grounds LLM outputs in verified external enterprise data by embedding documents, performing vector similarity search, and injecting top matches into the prompt context.
ai_tech_interview.analogy: Like taking an open-book exam where you look up exact textbook passages before writing an answer, rather than trying to guess from distant memory.

scenario.title: Knowledge Retrieval: Pure Hallucination vs Grounded RAG

steps.action: Asks question about internal company vacation policy
steps.annotation: Private policy unknown to training set

steps.action: Hallucinates plausible yet completely fabricated policy numbers
Submits query to enterprise assistant
Retrieves top-k policy chunks and constructs augmented prompt
Generates factual response with direct document citation

code_sample.code:
def rag_query(user_query, vector_store, llm_client):
    # 1. Retrieve relevant verified context chunks
    relevant_chunks = vector_store.similarity_search(user_query, k=3)
    context_text = '\n\n'.join([c.page_content for c in relevant_chunks])
    
    # 2. Augment prompt with grounded context
    prompt = f'Use the following context to answer:\n{context_text}\n\nQuery: {user_query}'
    return llm_client.generate(prompt=prompt)

explanation_lines.note: Performs top-k vector cosine similarity search
Injects verified context into strict prompt template

comparison_table.option_a: Fine-Tuning: Frozen at model training cut-off date
comparison_table.option_b: RAG: Real-time updates by updating vector database

comparison_table.option_a: Fine-Tuning: Black-box neural weights without citations
comparison_table.option_b: RAG: Direct chunk citations and page references

comparison_table.option_a: Fine-Tuning: High GPU compute and data curation costs
comparison_table.option_b: RAG: Lightweight embedding and vector index storage

takeaways: RAG solves LLM hallucination and training cutoff limitations without model retraining.
Chunking strategy and embedding model choice heavily dictate retrieval quality.
Use hybrid search (BM25 lexical + dense vectors) for production domain accuracy.
common_mistakes: Using RAG when the problem requires teaching the model new reasoning or style.
Ignoring chunk boundary fragmentation that cuts off critical sentence context.
Failing to implement reranking (e.g. Cohere rerank) after initial vector retrieval.

security_engineering.concept_summary: L'authentification à deux facteurs (2FA) exige des preuves d'identité issues de deux catégories distinctes. Présenter deux éléments d'une même catégorie ne constitue pas un 2FA.
security_engineering.analogy: Comme ouvrir un coffre-fort nécessitant à la fois une combinaison secrète (Connaissance) et une clé physique (Possession), et non deux combinaisons successives.

scenario.title: Authentification 2FA: Vérification de l'Indépendance des Facteurs

variants.label: Sans Séparation de Catégorie (Mot de passe + Question secrète)

steps.action: Envoie le mot de passe principal
Demande la réponse à la question de sécurité
Fournit le nom de son animal d'enfance
Refuse la session: deux facteurs de même catégorie

variants.label: Avec 2FA Authentique (Mot de passe + Clé physique FIDO2)

steps.action: Envoie le mot de passe du compte
Envoie un défi cryptographique
Signe le défi en touchant sa clé FIDO2
Valide les deux catégories distinctes et émet le jeton JWT

explanation_lines.note: Collecte les catégories valides (Connaissance, Possession, Inhérence)
Rejette si les deux facteurs appartiennent à la même catégorie

comparison_table.option_a: Mot de passe, code PIN, question secrète
comparison_table.option_b: Vulnérable au phishing et à l'ingénierie sociale

comparison_table.option_a: Clé FIDO2, badge physique, application TOTP
comparison_table.option_b: Exige un accès direct à un équipement physique
Inhérent aux caractéristiques biologiques de l'individu

takeaways: Le 2FA exige des catégories distinctes, pas deux mots de passe successifs.
Les SMS OTP sont sensibles au SIM-swapping; préférez WebAuthn/FIDO2.
En entretien, structurez toujours votre réponse autour des 3 piliers d'authentification.
common_mistakes: Confondre vérification en deux étapes et authentification multi-facteurs authentique.
Considérer le SMS OTP comme équivalent à une clé physique FIDO2.
Oublier de nommer les trois catégories: Connaissance, Possession, Inhérence.

security_engineering.concept_summary: Zwei-Faktor-Authentifizierung (2FA) erfordert Identitätsnachweise aus zwei voneinander unabhängigen Kategorien. Mehrere Faktoren aus derselben Kategorie genügen nicht.
security_engineering.analogy: Wie eine Tresortür, die sowohl eine Zahlenkombination (Wissen) als auch einen physischen Schlüssel (Besitz) erfordert, nicht zwei getrennte Zahlenfolgen.

steps.action: Sendet primäres Benutzerpasswort
Fordert Beantwortung einer Sicherheitsfrage an
Sendet Namen des Haustiers
Verweigert Zugriff: zwei Faktoren derselben Kategorie
Sendet Benutzerpasswort
Übermittelt kryptografische Challenge-Nonce
Signiert Challenge durch Berühren des FIDO2-Tokens
Bestätigt zwei unabhängige Faktoren und erteilt Sitzungstoken

comparison_table.option_b: Erfordert physische Kontrolle über das Gerät

takeaways: 2FA verlangt unterschiedliche Kategorien, nicht lediglich zwei Passwörter.
SMS-OTP ist durch SIM-Swapping angreifbar; FIDO2 bietet Phishing-Resistenz.
Im Vorstellungsgespräch die drei Kernkategorien Wissen, Besitz und Inhärenz nennen.
common_mistakes: SMS-Nachrichten die gleiche Sicherheit wie FIDO2-Hardwaretokens zuschreiben.
Die drei Authentifizierungskategorien im Gespräch nicht präzise trennen.
